need: Cover and title page of Homer Hoyt's One Hundred Years of Land Values in Chicago, University of Chicago Press, 1933 (Internet Archive scan, public domain).
shows: No public-domain cover or title-page scan of Hoyt's 1933 book is available on Wikimedia Commons. The Internet Archive holds the volume but its page scans are not mirrored to Commons under a usable license, and the fetcher is Commons-only. Needs a manual Internet Archive grab if required.

need: Page scan of Hoyt's table ranking races and nationalities by effect on land values, from the 1933 book.
shows: Not found as a public-domain file on Commons. The specific ranking-table page is not on Commons; would have to be extracted from an Internet Archive scan of the book directly.

need: Portrait photograph of economist Homer Hoyt.
shows: No public-domain portrait of Homer Hoyt found on Commons across several query phrasings (economist, land economist, real estate). Skipped.

need: Portraits of University of Chicago sociologists Robert E. Park and Ernest Burgess (Robert E. Park half).
shows: Period black-and-white studio portrait of an elderly bespectacled white man in a suit, consistent with sociologist Robert E. Park. Commons file File:Robert E. Park.jpg, Public domain.

need: Portraits of University of Chicago sociologists Robert E. Park and Ernest Burgess (Ernest Burgess half).
shows: No usable portrait of sociologist Ernest W. Burgess found on Commons. A file named Burgess.jpg turned out to be an RAF war-grave headstone for a different Burgess (deleted). Burgess portrait skipped.

need: Ernest Burgess concentric-zone diagram of Chicago (the classic urban-ecology rings).
shows: Not found as a public-domain file on Commons. A file named Burgess Model L was a biplane aircraft, not the concentric-zone diagram (deleted). The canonical concentric-ring diagram redrawings on Commons are not under a clearly free license that the fetcher accepts. Skipped.

need: 1934 federal or newspaper announcement of the Federal Housing Administration / National Housing Act.
shows: No public-domain FHA / National Housing Act 1934 announcement, letterhead, or poster found on Commons across several phrasings. Skipped.

need: Scan of the FHA Underwriting Manual, 1938 edition, showing the incompatible racial groups and adverse influences passages.
shows: No public-domain page scan of the 1938 FHA Underwriting Manual found on Commons. Excerpt scans circulate via Arlington County and the Bill of Rights Institute but are not on Commons under a fetchable license. Skipped.

need: HOLC residential security map of Chicago (Mapping Inequality / National Archives) showing A green through D red zones (existing asset reused).
shows: HOLC Residential Security Map of Chicago, c.1940, with the A/B/C/D color grading. Existing credits.json asset (File:Holc-chicago.jpg, CC0). Note: this id is misnamed 'homer-hoyt' but is in fact the Chicago HOLC map.

need: HOLC residential security map of Chicago showing A green through D red zones (second existing asset, modern reconstruction).
shows: Modern data reconstruction of HOLC neighborhood redlining grades for Chicago. Existing credits.json asset (File:Home Owners' Loan Corp. (HOLC) Neighborhood Redlining Grade in Chicago, Illinois.png, CC BY-SA 4.0). Reused.

need: A HOLC residential security map example for the national-spread montage (It Spread To A Nation beat).
shows: Genuine 1938 HOLC Residential Security Map of Brooklyn, New York, on a Hagstrom street base, with First/Second/Third/Fourth-grade color legend (green/blue/yellow/red). Federal-government original; Mapping Inequality release is public domain. Serves as a non-Chicago HOLC example for the national-machine beat; NOT a Chicago map.

need: A HOLC area-description sheet for a Chicago South Side district with the surveyor's notes.
shows: No public-domain HOLC area-description sheet (the clearance/notes form) for a Chicago South Side district found on Commons. A residential-security map that surfaced was Denver, not a Chicago description sheet (deleted). Skipped.

need: Photograph of a Chicago South Side / Black Belt street in the late 1930s (existing asset reused).
shows: Russell Lee, FSA, 1941, Chicago South Side Black Belt scene. Existing credits.json asset (File:Chicagoblackbelt.jpg, Public domain, Library of Congress). Reused; also available as id color-line-5.

need: Photograph of a Chicago South Side / Black Belt street in the late 1930s (second existing asset reused).
shows: Russell Lee, FSA, 1941, Linotype operators of the Chicago Defender, South Side Chicago. Existing credits.json asset (Public domain, Library of Congress ppmsca.01614). Reused as period South Side imagery.

need: Photograph of Carl A. Hansberry, Black Chicago real estate broker.
shows: Studio portrait of Carl Augustus Hansberry, Chicago real estate broker and father of Lorraine Hansberry, dated 1940. NYPL Digital Collections, Public domain. Correctly depicts Carl Hansberry.

need: Photograph of the Hansberry three-flat at 6140 South Rhodes Avenue or the Washington Park subdivision (existing asset reused).
shows: The Lorraine Hansberry House, the Chicago landmark three-flat tied to the Hansberry family. Existing credits.json asset (File:Lorraine Hansberry House.jpg, CC BY-SA 4.0). Reused for the Rhodes Avenue / Washington Park block.

need: Portrait of a young Lorraine Hansberry.
shows: No public-domain portrait of Lorraine Hansberry found on Commons. Queries returned her New York apartment building, not a portrait (deleted). Most Hansberry portraits remain under copyright. Skipped.

need: Exterior of the United States Supreme Court, circa 1940.
shows: Front elevation of the United States Supreme Court Building at dusk, columns lit. Correct subject and building (completed 1935, unchanged exterior), but a modern color photograph, not a circa-1940 image. CC BY-SA 3.0, Joe Ravi. Usable as the SCOTUS exterior; note it is present-day, not period.

need: Photograph of the Shelley house on Labadie Avenue, St. Louis.
shows: Two-story brick rowhouse at 4600 Labadie Avenue, St. Louis, the Shelley House National Historic Landmark, with the bronze landmark plaque visible in the front yard. CC BY 3.0. Correct subject.

need: Portraits of attorneys Thurgood Marshall and Loren Miller (Thurgood Marshall half).
shows: No usable public-domain or CC portrait of Thurgood Marshall found on Commons across several phrasings. Most are rights-reserved. Skipped.

need: Portraits of attorneys Thurgood Marshall and Loren Miller (Loren Miller half).
shows: Period photograph of Loren Miller, civil-rights attorney and later Los Angeles County Superior Court judge. CC BY 4.0, Los Angeles Times. Correct subject.

need: Modern scan of a Chicago property deed showing a racially restrictive covenant clause still printed in the text (existing asset reused as a covenant document).
shows: Period 'Only Members of the Caucasian Race' restrictive-covenant advertisement (Kimball & Richards, Land Merchants). Existing credits.json asset (File:Exclusionary Covenants.jpg, Public domain). It is a genuine racially restrictive covenant document but is a Salt Lake City Highland Park promotion, NOT a Chicago deed scan. Reused as a stand-in for the covenant-clause visual; an actual Chicago deed scan was not found public-domain on Commons.
